# `oaap app access`

a time-boxed access into one instance network (RFC-0044). 'wireguard' needs node profile 'remote-access' and its firewall fence is not measured on a real node yet.

**Root:** needs `sudo`.

## Usage

```sh
oaap app access [--shape {forward,wireguard}] [--holder HOLDER]
                       [--hours {1,8,24}] [--service SERVICE] [--port PORT]
                       [--endpoint ENDPOINT]
                       {open,close,list,sweep} [name]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | what to do -- see Actions below |
| `name` | open/list: the instance; close: the access id |
| `--shape SHAPE` | open: forward (default) or wireguard (one of `forward`, `wireguard`) |
| `--holder HOLDER` | open: who the access is for (default: you) |
| `--hours HOURS` | open: how long (default 8) (one of `1`, `8`, `24`) |
| `--service SERVICE` | open --shape forward: the service name |
| `--port PORT` | open --shape forward: the port |
| `--endpoint ENDPOINT` | open --shape wireguard: the address the peer will dial (this node's own reachable name) |

## Actions

Whether an action needs `sudo` is read from the rule the node enforces, with the other arguments left out (e.g. `node care` reads, `node care measure` needs `sudo`).

| Action | Needs `sudo` |
|---|---|
| `open` | yes |
| `close` | yes |
| `list` | yes |
| `sweep` | yes |
